v1.feedback: The oompah-as-breathing-rhythm interpretation is genuinely inventive — the 5.5s rest→swell→snap envelope and the cool-sage-to-tarnished-brass palette crossfade give the Aizawa form a musical heartbeat without breaking its recognizable topology. Two refinements: the particle swell factor (1 + pulse*0.12) combined with size boost (1 + pulse*0.3) may push outer lobes past frame at peak oom on narrow viewports — clamp or pull the camera back ~10%; and the brass-moment brightness bump (+0.15) is subtle enough to miss on many monitors, so consider also slightly shifting the background color (e.g. 0x07090c → 0x0a0b0e) during pah to make the tonal swerve land harder as a felt room-tone change rather than just a particle tint.

v2.feedback: The oompah breathing envelope is well-conceived — sage-to-brass crossfade on a 5.5s cycle reads as a genuine tonal swerve rather than a gimmick. Two refinements: the swell push (`away * uSwell * 0.35`) dilates the attractor uniformly, which softens the Aizawa's characteristic double-lobe silhouette at peak OOM — consider scaling swell anisotropically (stronger along z, weaker in xy) to preserve the butterfly profile during the beat. Second, the PAH snap-back could benefit from a brief particle-size contraction (sizeMul dipping to ~0.85 before returning to 1.0) to give the release a rhythmic 'thump' the eye can feel, right now the settle phase is too smooth and the oompah reads more as breathing than brass-band punctuation.
